newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi defence head in Geneva on way to Washington.
newsitem.headline: Saudi defence head in Geneva on way to Washington.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Sultan, who has arrived in Geneva on his way to the United States, was on Sunday quoted as saying he would not sign any arms deals while in Washington.

The official Saudi Press Agency reported early on Sunday that Prince Sultan, accompanied by Commerce Minister Osama Ibrahim Faqih and Oil Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi, arrived in Geneva on Saturday. It gave no details.
Saudi newspapers reported that Prince Sultan would travel to Washington on Monday for talks with President Bill Clinton and senior U.S. officials.
On March 5, he will leave for Paris for talks with French President Jacques Chirac, they added.
Asked by the Saudi Okaz newspaper whether he planned to sign any arms deal in Washington, Prince Sultan said: "This matter is out of the question."

Diplomats in Saudi Arabia had described as "uneasy" Prince Sultan's upcoming talks in Washington, expected to cover a June bombing which killed 19 U.S. soldiers in the Eastern Province, a potential sale of U.S. fighters to Riyadh and Middle East peace.

Prince Sultan told Okaz he would discuss "the strategy of the U.S. administration towards Arab peace and our (Gulf) region and our relationship with America in all its aspects and find out if there is any change in the administration's strategy".
Prince Sultan was on Saturday quoted as saying a Saudi probe into the June bombing was continuing but he remained tight-lipped on the progress of the investigation.
The talks are set against the backdrop of official American complaints that the Saudis are not telling Washington enough about the bombing probe.
The diplomats said they expected the U.S. administration to press for more information on the bombing.
U.S. media reports have alleged that the Saudi authorities have uncovered Iranian involvement in the blast.
Iran denied the allegations and Saudi Arabia, describing the reports as unfounded, said only that it had full details and would reveal them when the investigation was completed.
